findings_qualitative.value: Ring gas is blueshifted ≲1 km/s relative to protostar, with possible expansion; asymmetric velocity, not a symmetric bubble.

claims.hypothesis: A distinctive gas ring exists around IRS 2 that is not explained by outflows or streamers
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 6 C18O(2-1) mosaic with moment, channel and PV analysis
claims.result: ~7,000 au diameter ring centered ~5,000 au from the protostar, blueshifted ≲1 km/s
claims.finding: Ring is unlike known outflow or streamer features

evidence.quote: the rings found in this IRS 2 system do not resemble structures or phenomena well known from previous observations of protostellar envelopes

claims.hypothesis: The ring is a magnetic wall from magnetic flux advection by interchange instability
claims.experiment: Compare ring size, location, and expansion timescale with theory
claims.result: Expansion at ~0.3 km/s gives ~1e5 yr, consistent with Class 0 timescale
claims.finding: Plausible, preliminary evidence of flux leakage; theory calculations still needed

evidence.quote: we conclude that the ALMA-resolved gas distribution of the IRS 2 ring is likely a product of the advection of the magnetic flux due to the interchange instability.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Outflow rejected because ring velocity is too small and no high-velocity component >~5 km/s; streamer rejected because SO connection only near systemic velocity

evidence.quote: the observed relative velocity of the C$^{18}$O ring with respect to the protostar is too small for the outflow interpretation

limitations_admitted.value: Ring may be a coincidental line-of-sight cloud component; theoretical calculations needed.

evidence.quote: it cannot be completely ruled out that the ring structure is just a coincidence of unrelated line-of-site components

referee_caveats_inferred: No modelling or simulation specific to IRS 2 supports the magnetic wall interpretation
